title: gxw-2001-unified
label: Marcus Johnson

won.source: How he won the title is not documented in this wing's own record; billed "'The Hero' Marcus Johnson (C)" defending against Eric Davis in the promotion's own earliest attested Front Office lineup announcement, 15 October 2001.

note: The earliest titleholder this wing's own record attests for this championship.

title: gxw-2001-unified
label: Dan Ryan

won.source: Not from a marked lineup line: a later in-story promo (the held record's December 2002 material) describes Dan Ryan as having held the GXW Unified World Heavyweight Championship for about nine months before losing it around the time of the promotion's Fallout 2002 pay-per-view.

note: Graded presumed rather than primary-source: sourced to an in-character promo's own recap rather than a marked lineup line. A separate primary source, the promotion's own year-end staff retrospective (posted January 2003), independently narrates this same reign as Ryan's second Unified World Title win of 2002 -- "winning it back a week later... then holding it until Fallout" -- following an earlier January 2002 reign and a brief loss to Eric Edwards in between, both now carried as their own reign rows on this title.

title: gxw-2001-unified
label: Dan Ryan

won.source: Not from a marked lineup line: the promotion's own year-end staff retrospective (posted January 2003) states Dan Ryan held this championship twice during 2002, "first winning in January, losing it several weeks later, winning it back a week later... then holding it until Fallout," the last show of the year.

note: This wing's own earlier lineup announcements do not mark a title change between Marcus Johnson and this first Ryan reign; a title picture gap this pass did not otherwise close.

title: gxw-2001-unified
label: Eric Edwards

won.source: Billed "Eric Edwards (champion)" defending against Dan Ryan and Marcus Johnson in the promotion's own Front Office lineup announcement for its Genesis pay-per-view, 28 February 2002.

note: The promotion's own year-end staff retrospective (see the prior reign's own source) states Ryan "won it back a week later" and held the title until Fallout, the last show of 2002 -- consistent with this reign ending at or shortly after Genesis, though no marked lineup line records the change directly.

title: gxw-2001-television
label: Chris Lehew

won.source: Not from a marked lineup line: the promotion's own year-end staff retrospective (posted January 2003) credits a heel stable led by Rob Sampson with "stablemate Jeffrey Roberts winning Lehew's TV title," placing Lehew as an earlier holder. Consistent with the promotion's own Fallout pay-per-view lineup (8 December 2001), which bills a First Blood Match for the Television Title between Jeffrey Roberts and Chris Lehew without marking a champion.

note: How or when Lehew first won the title is not documented in this wing's own record.

title: gxw-2001-television
label: Jeffrey Roberts

won.source: The promotion's own year-end staff retrospective (posted January 2003) states Jeffrey Roberts won Chris Lehew's Television Championship as part of Rob Sampson's heel stable's own storyline; dated to circa the Fallout pay-per-view (8 December 2001), the only lineup this wing's own record shows the two wrestling for this title.

note: Graded presumed rather than primary-source: sourced to the staff retrospective's own account rather than a marked lineup line.

title: gxw-2001-television
label: Rob Sampson

won.source: The promotion's own year-end staff retrospective (posted January 2003) states Rob Sampson "went on to win that same title himself, later holding it along with the Continental title simultaneously" during 2002, before this wing's own next marked Television titleholder (The Reaver, attested July 2002).

note: How or when Sampson won the title from Roberts is not documented in this wing's own record; this reign ends by July 2002, when The Reaver is the next marked titleholder this wing's own record attests.

title: gxw-2001-television
label: The Reaver

won.source: Billed "The Reaver" defending the Television Championship in a stated rematch at the held record's earliest Onslaught card.

note: How he first won the title is not documented in the held record.

won.source: Billed "'Mr. Main Event' Rob Sampson (C)" at Battleground Britain (2002); confirmed still champion three months later at an X-perience card, March 2003.

title: gxw-2001-continental
label: Kendall Codine

won.source: The promotion's own year-end staff retrospective (posted January 2003) states Kendall Codine "went on to capture the Continental title and hold it for a good portion of the year" during 2002, in a feud it separately names as the promotion's own Feud of the Year against Rob Sampson.

note: The same retrospective credits Sampson with holding the Continental title "as of this writing" (January 2003), consistent with this wing's own existing primary-source reign for Sampson (billed champion at Battleground Britain, December 2002) succeeding this one; how or when the title changed hands between them is not documented in this wing's own record.

won.source: Billed "'The American Nightmare' Gabriel Bane (C)" in a Japanese Death Match at Battleground Britain (2002).
Billed "former GXW X-Treme Champ Black" in a December 2003 tournament-round announcement; his win and loss are not otherwise documented in the held record.

title: gxw-2001-xtreme
label: Clapper

won.source: Billed "GXW's Xtreme Champion Clapper" the same December 2003 week, and explicitly "Clapper (c)" defending in a three-way at Battleground Britain (2004) the following month.

note: The last titleholder this corpus attests for this championship.

title: gxw-2001-tag
label: Motor City Maniacs

won.source: How or when the Motor City Maniacs won this title is not documented in this wing's own record; billed "The Motor City Maniacs vs. True Living Colors" for the World Tag Team Titles in the promotion's own Fallout pay-per-view lineup (8 December 2001), and confirmed still champions by the Cruiserweight-division staffer's own retirement announcement for the team, 14 January 2002 ("they are still your current GXW Tag Team Champions").

note: The team's own characters retired from the promotion the same week this reign is last attested, leaving the title's own status unresolved in this wing's own record; the promotion's next marked Tag Team titleholder is the Night Cripplers, attested December 2002.

won.source: Billed "The Night Cripplers (C)" defending against the Assassins and the Monsta Boyz at Battleground Britain (2002).

title: gxw-2001-womens
label: Jennifer Rowe

won.source: Billed "'The Blonde Bomber' Jennifer Rowe (C)" defending the renamed GWE Women's Championship on the promotion's first card under its new name; two earlier matches in the held record (a October 2003 Towel Match and a March 2004 Revolution title match) also contest this championship without a marked incumbent in their own announcement lines.

note: The only titleholder this corpus attests by a marked lineup line for this championship.

title: gxw-2001-unified
label: Zero

won.source: First and only marked appearance in the held record: billed "Zero (C)" defending in a triple threat at the held record's Battleground Britain (2002) pay-per-view.

note: No later title match in the held record names Zero as champion or challenger; John Miller is the next holder this corpus attests, by October 2003.

title: gxw-2001-unified
label: John Miller

won.source: Presumed from context, not a marked lineup line: Miller is a participant (unmarked) in an October 2003 Unified Championship match, and is explicitly billed "'Steel City Icon' John Miller (c)" defending the same title three months later at Battleground Britain (2004).

note: Graded presumed for the October 2003 win specifically; the January 2004 title-holder billing is a marked, primary-source fact.

title: gxw-2001-unified
label: Boogie Smallz

won.source: Billed "Boogie Smallz (C)" defending the renamed GWE Unified World Heavyweight Championship on the promotion's first card under its new name, one week after challenging Miller for the same title at Battleground Britain (2004) with no stated result read.

note: The last titleholder this corpus attests for this championship.

won.source: Billed "Kin Hiroshi (champion)" two and a half weeks later, defending against Hellfighter; no title-change match between the two is captured.

Billed "(C) Boogie Smallz" defending in a Table Match; confirmed still champion through at least three further shows into January 2003 (Fallout 2002, Battleground Britain 2002, and a 4 January 2003 Onslaught defense).

title: gxw-2001-television
label: Stephen Waltz

won.source: Billed "Stephen Waltz (c)" defending at Battleground Britain (2004); Waltz was also billed FIRST -- this corpus's own consistent marked-champion convention -- in unmarked Television title matches running from June through October 2003, suggesting a longer reign this corpus does not otherwise mark.

note: Confirmed still champion at the promotion's first card under the renamed 'GWE' banner, April 2004 -- the last titleholder this corpus attests.

title: gxw-2001-continental
label: Boogie Smallz

won.source: Billed "GXW Continental Champ Smallz" in a December 2003 tournament-round announcement; how or when he won the title from Sampson is not documented in the held record.

note: The last titleholder this corpus attests for this championship.

won.source: Not from a marked lineup line: the promotion's own year-end staff retrospective (posted January 2003) credits its own Stable of the Year, Extreme Tendencies, with claiming multiple titles during 2002 including "Inferno winning the Cruiserweight title."

title: gxw-2001-tag

note: The last titleholder this corpus attests for this championship.

title: gxw-2001-tv-tag
label: Insane Pain

won.source: How or when Insane Pain won this title is not documented in this wing's own record; billed "Insane Pain (C)" defending against Wicked Sight and Billy Moser in the promotion's own earliest attested Front Office lineup announcement (15 October 2001), and again contesting the title against Fast Lane at the Fallout pay-per-view (8 December 2001).

note: The only titleholder this wing's own record attests for this championship, which is not mentioned again in this wing's own record after December 2001; it may have been folded into the main World Tag Team title line, but nothing this pass read confirms that either way.
